cross_response_observations: The eight responses exhibit several shared defect patterns across multiple models. The most prevalent error is the assumption of period-2 alternation (even=P, odd=N), appearing in responses A and G, which stems from misunderstanding the role of move 1 in the game. Move-set errors are common: Response B drops 1 (treating 2^0 as empty power), while Response F expands to all integers up to 100 (confusing powers-of-two with numbers representable as sums of powers). Framework confusion appears in three forms: Response E computes Grundy numbers via mex instead of direct P/N; Response G inappropriately applies Nim XOR rule; and Responses C and D mishandle P/N conventions (C swaps globally, D only sets base case wrong). Pattern heuristics without DP verification appear in A, B, and G, where models assert periodic patterns without computing reachable positions. Truncation issues affect D (64 chars), E (30 chars), and F (100 chars). The non-terminating Response H loops infinitely without producing output. Notably, no response correctly identifies the actual period-3 structure (P at positions divisible by 3), and none produce the correct 101-character classification string. All eight responses fail verification, demonstrating systematic weaknesses in combinatorial game analysis including move-set comprehension, base-case handling, and DP execution.
